why: This is tree serialization for N-ary trees: preorder alone is ambiguous, but writing each node with its child count makes it self-delimiting, just like null markers do for binary trees. Deserializing reads a node, then recursively reads exactly childCount subtrees.
hints: In the wire format, how do you know where one node's children end and its next sibling starts?

The child count tells you exactly how many complete subtrees follow. So decoding is: read value:count, then decode count subtrees in order. Parsing the text form is the same idea with parentheses and commas as the delimiters.

Use an explicit stack for both directions (a stack of nodes with remaining child slots for the wire format, a stack of open parents for the text form). Each node is handled O(1) times: O(total nodes).
pitfalls: A leaf prints without parentheses: 42, not 42().
Values can have several digits (10, 1000000000), so parse whole numbers, not single characters.
Child order matters: keep children in the order they appear.
Trees can be 2,000 deep; recursion needs a raised limit.
